Grace was stunning in the dress, so stunning it gave Coolidge a pause. It was one thing for his wife to be his ambassador, another for her to be glamorous; he did not like to admit it, but it irked him to have Grace so available to the world. Did the dress in the painting have to be so red? Could it not be another color? The artist told Calvin it had to be red; contrast was important because the red set off the white dog.
